reason: No specific prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises. Claims about microstructural descriptor–property correlations, baseline simulation errors, and the mediating role of the heterostructure in HfNbTiVAl10 are presented without supporting references, leaving all premises unsupported.
premises: Microstructural descriptors (volume fraction, size, spatial arrangement of secondary phases) can be reliably quantified from SEM/TEM of HfNbTiVAl10.
These descriptors correlate strongly with Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior in this alloy.
A hybrid ML–physics model using these descriptors can bypass the high computational cost of full atomistic simulations.
Conventional full-scale DFT or interatomic potential simulations have errors of 20–30% for these properties.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates load transfer and crack deflection, governing macroscopic behavior.
